scope: Open review of static lung volumes and how they are interpreted, including why spirometry cannot measure residual volume, FRC, or total lung capacity.

keyRecommendations.text: Static volumes are tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volume. Capacities include inspiratory capacity, FRC, vital capacity, and TLC.
RV, FRC, and TLC cannot be measured with a simple spirometer. They are measured by radiology, plethysmography, or gas dilution (helium dilution or nitrogen washout).
Static volumes matter for both obstructive and restrictive defects. Air trapping correlates positively with RV, FRC, TLC, and RV/TLC.

clinicalBottomLine: Do not try to read residual volume or total lung capacity off a spirometer. Use plethysmography or gas dilution, and interpret a high RV/TLC as air trapping in obstruction.
notableCaveats: The 2019 spirometry performance standard is kept as source-spirometry.txt. These questions use the open review of static lung volumes, which is what the catalogue title asks for beyond manoeuvre quality.

source.title: The physiological basis and clinical significance of lung volume measurements.
